title: Asado-style grilled flank steak
summary: Flank steak salted generously with coarse salt and cooked over a hot wood or charcoal fire, sliced thin across the grain.

ingredients.note: one or two steaks, about 2.5 cm (1 in) at the thickest
optional; many asadores use salt alone

steps: Take the steak out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and pat it dry.
Build a hot fire of hardwood charcoal or wood embers and let it burn down until the coals are covered in white ash; you should be able to hold your hand above the grate for only 2–3 seconds.
Salt the steak on both sides just before it goes on the fire.

Grill 5–7 minutes a side, turning once, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 54–57 °C (130–135 °F) for medium-rare. Move it to a cooler part of the grill if the outside chars before the centre is ready.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain at an angle. Season with pepper if using and serve with lemon wedges.
Indoors, use a smoking-hot cast-iron pan or grill pan with the same timings and the fan on.
tips: Slicing across the grain matters more with flank than with any other steak: with the grain it chews like rope.
Serve with chimichurri from the sauces chapter.

origin.history: Asado grew out of the cattle culture of the gauchos on the Pampas, who roasted beef over open fires from the 1700s onward. It is now a social occasion as much as a method: an asador tends a parrilla of embers, and the meat is seasoned with little but coarse salt. Vacío, a cut from the flank, is a staple of the grill, and flank steak is its nearest supermarket match.
